title: Don’t Miss This Great New Action Game Inspired By From Software’s Earliest Series
description: Amid the countless games flooding Steam at all times, a new release this week is not to be missed: Queen's Domain. The action-adventure game from Freshly Baked Games takes more than a little inspiration from the earliest titles made by From Software, the King's Field series, but it manages to stand out from other modern fantasy games. That's the takeaway from senior producer Jean-Luc Seipke, who goes into their impressions of the game in the video below. Jean-Luc is not a King's Field player but very much enjoyed the opening 10 hours of the game--an amount that somehow only equates to about 5% completion, according to an in-game counter. The gorgeous retro visuals evoke a game released somewhere right between the PlayStation 1 and 2 eras, and is light on story overall, although it leans into environmental storytelling in a way that feels very true to the style of From Software. Jean-Luc notes the gameplay may not properly sell why the game is such a joy to play. The combat is decidedly slower-paced than many other games, even requiring you to be at full stamina in order to deal damage. There's also no block or parry, instead requiring you to physically move out of the way of an attack to avoid damage. This results in a very deliberate style of combat, where you have to really pay attention to animations and be calculating with your every move. What interests me most from Jean-Luc's rundown is the exploration. You eventually unlock a weapon, the Holy Sword Endu, which provides you with the ability to dash forward or backward in mid-air and can be upgraded to provide additional charges. What initially might feel like a linear world becomes something far more dense and interesting as you recognize the way the sword progressively lets you reach more and more areas as you poke and prod at its environments to see where it can take you. You should be aware that it can be easy to lose progress, as there are no checkpoints or auto-saves. Die, and you're sent back to your…

title: "We didn't want the brooding hero out for revenge": How quiet lulls and a bird-sketching lead make Control Resonant a more introspective kind of action game
description: Like the repeating pattern effect afflicting its warped Manhattan, Control Resonant threw me for a loop. One minute I would be brutally slashing and smashing my way through hordes of inhuman enemies, enacting a never-ending chain combo of bellowing violence with my Aberrant, and the next minute I would be scanning nearby rooftops for signs of a squeaking purple dragon plushie to give to a very wiggly dog (who, I was pretty sure, could teleport). Combat often felt desperate and bloody; knockdown-and-drag-out brawls that had me limping away like John Wick after a particularly messy gunkata affair. Still, these fights all ended eventually, and in their place was not always more action-RPG battling but, more often, an odd sense of melancholic peace and quiet. It’s a strange dichotomy I’ve been thinking about nearly nonstop since I finished my first playthrough. Spoilers/Revelations for Control Resonant ahead. Don’t say we didn’t warn/notify you. title: Patrick Stewart Dies At 86
description: Beloved actor Patrick Stewart has died at the age of 86. The veteran of stage and screen was best known for his many years as Star Trek's Jean-Luc Picard and X-Men's Charles Xavier, though he also had notable roles in video games, including The Elder Scrolls IV: Oblivion and Castlevania: Lords of Shadow. "We announce with grew sorrow the passing of Sir Patrick Stewart yesterday at his home in Los Angeles, in the loving care of his beloved wife Sunny, following a brief and poignant journey with Alzheimer's Disease and Lewy Body Dimentia" a statement on his official Instagram reads. "He has been held in the warm embrace of family and friends, surrounded by live music, prayer, tears, laughter, and the kind of profound emotion that only he could inspire after a lifetime of devotion to us all. We will forever cherish the peaceful ease and reflection on his face, an enduring reminder of his invincible grace." Stewart's role as Picard made him a household name, and following the conclusion of Star Trek: The Next Generation, he reprised the role in several Star Trek films as well as the series Star Trek: Picard. Though best known for his live-action roles like Picard and Xavier, Stewart was also known for his iconic voice. Alongside the aforementioned games like Oblivion and Castlevania: Lords of Shadow (and its sequel), Stewart had voice roles in everything from American Dad to The Prince of Egypt. He also narrated the Ted movies, with his friend Ian McKellen taking over the role for the recent Ted series on Peacock.

title: WoW: Forever Won’t Have Dead Servers
description: World of Warcraft: Forever will avoid repeating WoW Classic's mistakes and will have tools to prevent "dead" or "unsustainable" server rulesets, Blizzard said. In the past, various WoW Classic servers became "dead" over time, as players either stopped playing or transferred to other servers. Those massive drops in population had major ramifications for players left on the server being unable to find groups for raids or dungeons, as well as for the server's economy and auction house. In some extreme cases, Blizzard gave away free character transfers so players could leave their "dead" servers behind. While Forever is going a different route with what are essentially mega servers tailored around specific rulesets, some players might still have anxiety when it comes to picking a ruleset that will be a healthy place to play long-term. In the latest episode of the WoW: Forever podcast, Blizzard said it has tools it can use if a ruleset's population becomes "unsustainable." Senior game designer Josh Greenfield gave the example of Forever's separate RP and (newly added) RP-PvP server rulesets. He said there were initially concerns about splitting up the RP community, fearing that one or both of the rulesets wouldn't be able to stand the test of time. He said Blizzard now believes "it will be fine," but does have options should the worst happen. "If someday down the line, if something happens and one or both of those populations can't quite sustain themselves, we have options if we do need to say link up their auction houses or allow them to group for instanced content," Greenfield said. Greenfield said it's not something Blizzard will jump to unless absolutely necessary and that it's committed to its current separate-ruleset path. Blizzard debated the idea of rulesets during Forever's development and discussed letting players from different rulesets group together for instanced content or combining auction houses. However, it landed on wanting to maintain distinct…

title: Artist With Music In GTA 6 Had No Idea About Any Of That
description: Cliff Richard is among the numerous famous artists who are lending their music to Rockstar's GTA 6, with Richard's classic tune "Devil Woman" appearing in the Netflix Extended Look. Richard, 86, didn't know about any of that, however, or that GTA 6 is a game and not a TV show. Speaking to The Times ( via Dexerto ), Richard said of the partnership with Rockstar for GTA 6: "I was told this happened!" He said his nephew's sons told him about it. "They didn't realize I could sing like that," he said. Lucia in GTA 6. Richard was eventually made aware of GTA 6, but the singer doesn't know what that is. “The show is a game show, isn’t it, really? One of the biggest on TV?” he asked. "Devil Woman" was originally released in 1976, so it's now 50 years old. Richard said he's pretty jazzed about the fact that young people will hear his music. “People will no longer just say, ‘Oh, Cliff Richard is from the past,’” he said. “Because I am, but that past is what makes everything what it is today." It was reported that Spotify streams of "Devil Woman" surged massively following the Netflix Extended Look in August. For more on the music of GTA 6, be sure to check out GameSpot's rundown of all the songs in the game. The game's official score by Justice is releasing on December 11, and it will be available to stream and buy on physical media. The same cannot be said for the game itself, which is a digital exclusive. The game will be sold at retailers, but there is no disc: just a code in a box. GTA 6 launches on November 19 for PS5 and Xbox Series X|S, and the game's file size is gargantuan.

title: Phantom Blade 0’s 66 Days Mode Is Brilliant
description: When I start action games, I typically start on harder difficulties, just so I can have the game push my limits and strategies a bit more. So when I first booted up Phantom Blade Zero, I was surprised to find that you do have the option to start on Wayfarer, Pathbreaker, or Hellwalker, aka: easy, medium, or hard, but not 66 Days mode. This initially confused me. Coming to a concession by starting on Hellwalker, I found that you can just switch difficulties whenever you like, which I’m sure can be for better or for worse, depending on who you talk to. But after 40 hours beating the game on Hellwalker, I wasn’t sure if the 66 Days mode would be worth replaying the game for. 66 Days mode is the same difficulty as Hellwalker, the hardest difficulty that I had already played, but with the added rule that you are locked into that difficulty and only have 66 lives. If you die 66 times, it's game over--permadeath. You have to start all over. Hesitant to go through the game all over again, I hovered over the option for a moment before curiosity got the better of me and I gave it a try. The first thing I noticed is that you get to keep all of your gear, all of your upgrades, all of your builds, but no quest items. This was surprising, as I thought you would start from scratch and work your way up again. But as I kept going, the second thing I noticed changed my impression. The moment I got hit for the first time, a switch flipped in my brain telling me, “Hey, don't f**k this up." This thought did not occur at all during my initial playthrough, as I would just mindlessly fly through swarms of trash mobs, and if I got sloppy and died, I’d just run back and clean up the rest of the mobs. This is the moment I understood 66 Days mode. In a sense, your first playthrough is a teacher who teaches you the tools on how to tackle the problems, and learning the history and stories. There’s no worry about asking questions or experimenting to see if something works; there’s no risk and…

title: Ubisoft Is Pumping The Brakes On Assassin’s Creed Remakes For Now
description: What's next for the Assassin's Creed franchise? Following the successful launch of Assassin's Creed Black Flag Resynced earlier this--which sold very well--you'd imagine that Ubisoft would be looking to fast-track another remake while it continues work on future titles. That's not the case, as Ubisoft dropped a new update on all things Assassin's Creed, including confirmation that it's not currently working on any remakes. "One thing we want to be transparent about today is that we currently have no other Assassin's Creed remake actively in development," Ubisoft wrote. "Our teams are already focused on the next chapter of Assassin's Creed titles, including projects you haven't heard about yet, featuring new settings and stories." While you shouldn't expect another Assassin's Creed remake anytime soon, Ubisoft added that it will still keep "exploring opportunities" to bring older titles back. As for future projects, Ubisoft said that it's making "good progress" on its darker Assassin's Creed experience, Codename Hexe. An update on it will arrive in 2027, and Ubisoft added that the team remains focused on delivering a "unique vision" at the heart of this project. The other in-development title, Codename Invictus, is also taking shape behind the scenes. This will be a multiplayer Assassin's Creed game, and Ubisoft says hundreds of players recently got to go hands-on with an early prototype. "One piece of feedback came through clearly though: Players saw great potential in the foundations but wanted more of the pillars that define Assassin's Creed. The team spent the past months acting on it, and Invictus is now evolving in an exciting direction that better reflects those pillars while staying true to its multiplayer ambitions," Ubisoft wrote. For current games, Black Flag Resynced players can download one final major update. This adds New Game Plus, Nightmare Mode, new rewards, finishers, trinkets, and additional customization options to the Black Flag remake.…

title: WoW: Forever Controller Support Is A First Step To Playing The MMO On “Whatever You Want”
description: World of Warcraft: Forever will launch with full controller support, a first for the various versions of Blizzard's longrunning PC-exclusive MMORPG. According to Blizzard, the option to play on controller is the "first leg of a journey" to make WoW playable "on whatever you want." Speaking to GamesRadar, WoW executive producer and vice president Holly Longdale said Blizzard's goal is to eventually have WoW playable "wherever you want, and, at some point, on whatever you want." The first step on that road, however, is ensuring controller support works really well. Blizzard is using the launch of Forever on November 4, the latest version of its MMO that reimagines the game's classic world and gameplay with new content and features, as a starting point. "Looking at where things are going when we hear about Project Helix [the codename for Xbox's next console], et cetera, I think platforms will be a bit more ubiquitous," Longdale said. She continued: "I think just doing some of the work we're doing on gamepad [support] is going to give players a lot of flexibility that I think goes beyond consoles." Having gone hands-on with Forever's controller support during BlizzCon 2026, I can say it works surprisingly well for a game that has been played almost exclusively with mouse and keyboard for 22 years. While modern WoW has added some barebones controller options in recent years, Forever's implementation is far superior, working seamlessly without the need for player-made addons like ConsolePort to make it usable. You have a surprisingly number of keybinds available at your fingertips (28, to be exact), making combat and interacting with quest NPCs a breeze. Inventory management and navigating menus is a little more cumbersome, but it does feel like a decent tradeoff for being able to play on a controller or a handheld, like the Xbox ROG Ally X. When WoW might be playable on something other than a PC remains to be seen, though Blizzard has made clear that if it were making a…

Depending on how much Aniimo you've played, you might not be able to access the island right away. In this guide, we'll explain exactly how to unlock Whisperwake Isles in Aniimo. Whisperwake Isles explained Crescent Bay in Whisperwake Isles Aniimo's Whisperwake Isles is an entirely new map to explore. This adds four new regions: Crescent Bay, Rosy Mirelands, Wildwater Gorge, and Cloudreach Falls. These areas offer new main story quests, puzzles, and plenty of exclusive new Aniimo to catch. If you're a new player, you won't be able to unlock this map right away, as there are a few prerequisites you must meet first. How to unlock Whisperwake Isles Whisperwake Isles map Access to Whisperwake Isles requires you to meet specific level and story requirements. Level-wise, you'll need to reach player level 55 and receive the Grade I Trailblazer promotion from Dr. Lewis. For the story requirements, you'll need to first complete the game's existing "Everlasting Echoback Song" Journey questline. This will unlock the season's new story quest called "A Tale of Tide and Song." If you've completed all of the launch missions in Aniimo, then you should automatically get a call from Dr. Lewis to continue the story. Completing A Tale of Tide and Song will unlock the questline called "A Song from the Sea." You'll need to complete this new quest in order to unlock the first region in Whisperwake Isles. This new Aniimo adventure begins in Crescent Bay, and continuing through the Whisperwake Isles missions will eventually lead you to the other three map regions. How to return to Whisperwake Isles There's a lot to explore within this new island map, but there's a good chance you'll want to return to the original map or visit your Aniimo Homeland.
